Okay, who wants to start? Start with the  microphone, please. Hi, Ruben. Congratulations.  
What did you make of the performance of your side?  It was a good result. I think if you look at both  
games, it was so much tougher than if you look  just to the results. We have so many weaknesses,  
and you can understand that in the game. But we  are fighting, and we managed to pass. I think we  
deserve, if you look at two games, to be in the  final. So good. Ruben, I know you've said that  
winning it won't mask a lot of things, but winning  it would surely give you and your team huge belief  
going forward, quite apart from the money that you  get, a trophy and tell everybody that you are on  
the right path. It's obviously the biggest game  that you've had since you've been. I think that  
is clear and I agree. The money is not the most  important. Even the title to win a title as a  
coach is that feeling. It's that feeling that we  can do good things, the feeling to give something  
to our fans, especially in this kind of season.  So I agree, it's not just playing Champions League  
next year, it's that feeling that we can change  things. Ruben, can I just ask you about Mason  
Mount? Because since you've arrived here, you've  always been so adamant that he'll be part of your  
plans and playing scores as a second goal, you  just have this massive grin on your face. Can you  
just talk to us about your feeling? Not just me.  If you look at the bench, that is the best thing.  
That is the best feeling as a coach. When you look  at the other guys on the bench and they are so  
happy for Mason Mount because everybody in that  dressing room see Mason Mount doing everything  
he can to be available. He's a really good player  and you can see both goals are really, really good  
goals. So I think not just Mason Mount, not just  me, but also the teammates, they were so happy for  
him. James. You've won major titles before, but if  you were to win this trophy in the context of this  
season, the difficulties you've had, where would  this rank among your achievements? Every coach  
will say that the next one is the most important.  I think it is the title with more exposure,  
but I cannot say that is the most important title.  I think your first one, I think, is more important  
because you want to establish you as a coach and  to win something, to say that you have a title,  
but it will be massive, especially after the  season in Premier League. So for me, it's the  
most important because it's the next one. Dave.  You said you would suffer tonight as a team, and  
that was the case, certainly in the first half. Do  you feel it will be a similar story in the final  
against Tottenham? We've beaten Manchester United  three times a season in all three games. And with  
that record, do you feel that your duo win over  them, that you and the fans will win over the  
final? Every game has its history. So we lost the  three last games, we can win this one. So if you  
look at the odds, we are closer to win than to  to lose. Both teams are going to play like all or  
nothing in this kind of game. It's quite similar.  The position of the coach is quite similar. I know  
that Ange has one more year. It is different,  the context, but we are struggling, both of us.  
So I don't know what is going to happen. That is a  good thing and a bad thing with this team. I never  
know. So I will try to prepare the the game, but I  think we are improving if we have more solutions.  
And you can see that we can take Garnacho that  gives us the speed, the transition for Amass,  
and to have that possibility can help us  to win games. Mason Mount, Kobbie Mainoo,  
all these players, we can choose from these  players and to prepare a final in a better  
way. So that we have to understand that this final  is completely different from Premier League games.  
What was your intention with the substitutions  with Mount and Amad and what did you make of their  
impact? I think they changed the games, but that  is credit to the players. What I felt that we need  
a little bit more energy. We had to keep the ball.  I think when you play with Mainoo and Casemiro,  
we win in some areas, but we lose a little bit in  the way we push forward the team. Bruno Fernandes  
is a really good player to drive the ball, but  also to start the play with long passes and that  
ability can help us. Amad is to change the Amad  because I felt that Garnacho was a little bit  
tired. It was my fault because he did a really  good job against Brentford. But we need to also  
to try to win games in Premier League. It's hard  to think about everything in this kind of game. So  
my thinking is always to help the team to win. To  follow on from that question, your substitutions  
have changed the game. Are they capable of playing  90 minutes on Sunday and indeed in Europe League  
finals? No, it's going to be hard. Players  like Mason Mount, we have to be careful. Amad  
is still getting his momentum. So some players  are not capable to do that. I felt Nouss,  
we rest Nouss, but you can feel it. Mazraoui  doesn't have the energy in this moment, so we'll  
try to help him in that department. Dalot is doing  everything to recover. And I think they will push  
now to be available. So some players cannot  play 90 minutes and you have to protect them  
to don't get injuries to the final. That  concludes the post-match press conference.
title: 'So many WEAKNESSES BUT WE ARE FIGHTING!' | Ruben Amorim | Man Utd 4-1 Athletic Bilbao (Agg 7-1)
